craft_notes: Sthāyin: vikalpa-sattarka-śakti unit 16 — vīrya-vimarśa of contested doctrine (owner reviews first-verse of chapter). Sanskrit-first: technical terms held (sattarka, dvaitādhivāsa, śaktipāta, codanā, akiṃcitkara); the twelve-fold kalana steps kept in order (u38). Rows: 1 (question-answer gait: nanu/maivam), 9 (verdicts line-final: na kiṃcit, akiṃcitkara), 2 (catalogues kept whole: śakti-names, kalana-ops), 6 (imperative close: ācaret). Close: cited-authority lines land flat. Rejected: softening the akiṃcitkara claim — killed: siddham is the text's word; attributing the kecit-view as fact — killed: u44's argument is contested, keep its hedged heat. Read aloud: cadence-checked — each negation and count lands on stress. Two-register split: how-then-practice closes as designed.

lines: For one rooted in consciousness, practice
is the fixing of breath, mind and body — like
is taken, nothing removed — how then practice?
l4.sanskrit_cite: saṃvidrūḍhasya prāṇabuddhidehaniṣṭhīkaraṇarūpo hi abhyāsaḥ bhārodvahanaśāstrārthabodhanṛttābhyāsavat saṃvidrūpe tu na kiṃcit ādātavyaṃ na apasaraṇīyam iti katham abhyāsaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is abhyāsa for the saṃvid-rooted? → Two registers: niṣṭhā-fixing (body-level) possible; saṃvid-level 'practice' is incoherent by definition.
c1_essence: Rooted-in-saṃvid: practice = fixing breath-mind-body; in saṃvid-form nothing taken or removed — how practice?
reads_against.c1_rasa: karuṇā with vīrya weight (compassion carrying fierce argument)
